item.title: [V2EX] [分享创造] 做了一个在浏览器里把照片转成十字绣图纸的小工具
item.description:
最近做了一个小工具 StitchFromPhoto 。

https://stitchfromphoto.com/

它可以把 JPG 、PNG 或 WebP 照片转成十字绣图纸。原图留在本地，浏览器用 Canvas 完成转换，不需要注册账号，也不会把照片上传到服务器。

转换用的是普通算法。浏览器先把图片缩到选定的针格尺寸，再匹配接近的 DMC 参考色，然后按使用频率压缩颜色。图纸宽度可以在 30 到 120 针之间调整，颜色数量是 6 到 36 种。完成后可以来回看彩色格子图和黑白符号图，页面也会计算不同 Aida 布目数下的成品尺寸。

制作、完整预览和线色表都能免费使用。导出高清 PNG 与分块 PDF 目前是每张图片 2.99 美元。同一张原图购买后，在当前浏览器里 24 小时内可以继续调整并重复导出，没有订阅。

现在还有一些限制。颜色匹配来自一份精简的数字 DMC 参考，只能作为近似结果，做大图前最好拿实体线比较。目前只支持全针，也没有逐格编辑。

如果有人愿意试一下，我最想知道黑白符号图在大尺寸图纸上够不够清楚。单张图片付费是否容易理解，也欢迎直接说。

item.title: [V2EX] [分享发现] 就营销事件而言，对 v 站现状尝试分析
item.description:
背景

看到这个我用 AI 给女朋友做了个抑郁测试，结果她朋友是前男友 。
顺到了这个很多人不是说不会推广和营销吗？站里就有现成案例，照着学就行。
于是了解到了 @t20000622yy 先生的

  • 为了让女朋友学 AI ，给她买了 MacBook Pro ，开了每月 200 刀的 GPT ，她却说我一直在压迫她
  • 大厂前端社招复盘
  • 盛大集团面经（专升本毕业 9 个月,99%代码靠 AI 写）

反思

这个《我用 AI 给女朋友做了个抑郁测试，结果她朋友是前男友》一帖，实话说我在看的时候其实感觉毫无违和。因为我觉得这里、其他地方，见到这样的人和内容，对我来说其实很自然。大家总是些有缺点的平常人，那方面之类的不太懂什么的很正常。
而这一帖读完之后，我觉得一般情况下，会有一种被愚弄的感觉，以及 @t20000622yy 先生的帖子，读完分析后，也会有一种被愚弄的感觉，进而产生气愤 => “站长！一定要把这样的封了！”。
但“当屋子里有一只蟑螂的时候，就意味着有一窝蟑螂”了。这帖这事是显眼的，是我们已经知道标准答案的了。对显眼的做一点处罚，不显眼的那些怎么办呢？

打假是一件需要成本的事情，全打不现实；不打变成劣币市场，没人愿意来。

而骗子是一定会存在的事情，没有骗子是违反自然规律的。因为骗意味着没有成本地获得能量，大自然奖励这样。
人类文明是对此的修正。

于是尝试从社区的角度，分析社区现状、发展策略。

分析工具与 prompt

硬性工具：Gemini 3.1 pro
软性工具：零阶道理 的概念
prompt 是放在 gem 里的。gem 里装的内容为

严格来说 ——
零阶道理，是在给定目标、时间尺度和比较对象之下，足以决定结论方向和主要量级的最小因果模型。。
这里有三个关键词。
1. 「方向」，它告诉你 A 和 B 到底哪个好；
2. 「量级」，它告诉你大概好多少 —— 是好百分之一，还是好十倍；须打分、百分比，让我知道程度。
3. 「最小」，它未必只含一个因素，但只保留最少的几个主导项，多一项都不要。

分析结果

由于时间问题，比如我要洗碗。所以我在大致浏览之后，确认没什么毛病，就不花精力自己提炼主要内容地这么贴上来了。
规模信任的零阶博弈道理
我觉得，这帖我站在了社区建设角度的这个大旗下，也许可以得到诸位的谅解，于是斗胆这么发出来了。

如果我的 prompt 顺带可以让一些人得益，也是很好的了。

item.title: [Level1Techs Forum] Hard hang on KVM switch-back (nvlddmkm error 14) - 4070 Ti + Odyssey G9 240Hz, wedges so deep even a scheduled shutdown won't go through
item.description:
KVM Model:

DP 1.4 dual monitor two pc

USB Interface (5-gigabit or 10-gigbit):

10 gigabit

Problem:

setup: 5900X (no iGPU), RTX 4070 Ti, Windows 11 Home, Samsung Odyssey G9 at 5120x1440/240Hz (so DSC) going through the DP 1.4 dual monitor 2-computer KVM. Second input is my work PC, which has literally never hiccuped once through this thing.

I’ve had this setup about 7 months. It was never 100% perfect - I’d get the occasional hang on switch once in a while and just lived with it. But two days ago it went from rare annoyance to nonstop. Now it hard-hangs constantly on switch-back to my main PC: G9 stays black, keyboard is lit but dead, only a power cut gets it back. Event log shows nvlddmkm error 14 at the exact second of the switch every single time (one incident escalated to error 153), then kernel-power 41 from me hitting the power button. At the worst of it I had five hangs inside 70 minutes.

The interesting part: the machine isn’t actually dead. I was in a Discord call with my headset receiver plugged straight into the PC (not through the KVM), and during a hang the audio would go silent while the KVM pointed at the main PC, then come back the moment I switched away. So the box is alive and the driver is just livelocked retraining the display. It’s stuck deep though - I set up an event-triggered task that force-restarts the GPU via pnputil when error 14 fires, and the restart-device call just times out. Even a scheduled shutdown /r sat blocked for 4+ minutes behind the wedged driver.

What I’ve ruled out so far, roughly in order:

- 240Hz/DSC link training: dropped to 120Hz, still hung

- A Corsair Xeneon Edge I’d installed the same day it got bad (HDMI direct to the GPU, not through the KVM): hangs happen with it completely unplugged too, although having it connected definitely makes hangs way more frequent, even powered off (guessing the driver still probes the connector during retrain)

- iCUE: killed the app and all Corsair services, still hung

- Driver/software state: uninstalled NVIDIA App, DDU in safe mode, clean driver-only install of 610.88. Bought me a completely clean day of switching, then it came back

- The KVM’s ports: it’s the dual monitor model and I only use one monitor, so I moved both my input and the G9 output over to the unused second channel. Hung on that channel too.

Two more data points I can’t explain away. It’s way worse in the afternoon than morning or evening, which makes me think something is heat-sensitive. And my work PC on the other input has stayed perfect through all of this, so the shared path (KVM output side, G9, that cable) seems fine, at least at whatever refresh the work PC negotiates.

Still on my list: swap DP cables between the two inputs, reseat the GPU and both PCIe power leads. But before I keep going - is the external power brick on these KVMs a known failure point? A sagging 5V rail shared across both columns is about the only thing left that fits the heat correlation, survives the channel swap test, and would explain why this was always slightly flaky but suddenly fell off a cliff. And has anyone seen a 40-series card get into this specific retrain livelock with a DSC monitor behind a KVM? Happy to pull logs or the memory dump if useful, I have the whole event log history from every incident.

I appreciate any insight you can all provide.

[Level1Techs Forum] Framework gets another data breach
item.description:
I got this email from Framework

framework email:

Dear Valued Framework Customer,

We are writing to inform you of a data breach at our business intelligence database provider Metabase that resulted in an attacker accessing customer names, email addresses, phone numbers, and addresses. Your information was in the database that was accessed in this breach. This breach did not include order or payment information.

We have full details on the incident below. We are deeply sorry for this breach of information, and are reviewing and improving our methodology for data storage in external database vendors.

We are also in the process of notifying the regulatory authorities in each region where relevant regulations exist. Note that while regulations in most regions do not require notification for breaches of names, email addresses, phone numbers, and addresses, we are sending this email to you regardless to ensure you have visibility and can take any actions needed.

What happened?

On August 6th, 2026 at 9am Pacific Time, Metabase notified us of a breach of their systems with the following email message:

On Monday, August 3, we discovered that Metabase Cloud was attacked by someone utilizing an unknown (“0-day”) security vulnerability in versions 1.58 and above. We immediately blocked the endpoints used for the attack, then quickly identified and patched the vulnerability. We notified law enforcement, and we have engaged with a third party forensics firm to conduct an independent investigation.

Your instance of Metabase was vulnerable to this 0-day. Therefore, to protect your company, we recommend you:

Rotate the credentials for every database connected to your instance; and

Review the admin accounts on your instance and remove anything you don’t recognize.

We also discovered that the attacker was able to gain access to your instance. We created a report on the actions we believe the attacker took on your instance, which includes log files, and which you can get from the Metabase Store at [removed url].

(If you do not have access to the Metabase Store, are having issues accessing the report, or do not want to click on a link in an unexpected email, you can log into your instance directly and reach us at Help > Get help in the grid menu in the upper right hand corner. We’ll confirm this message is from us and email you the report.)

This report is based on our own application logs. We did not query or read the data in your connected databases.

Depending on the jurisdictions in which you operate and kinds of data your instance connects to, you may have notification obligations under applicable laws. If you have concerns in this regard, we recommend you assess potential notification obligations with your company’s legal or compliance experts.

We regret any inconvenience this incident may cause you, and we are here to support you. If you have questions, please reply to this email or email us at [removed email address], and we’ll get back to you as quickly as we can.

Sameer Al-Sakran

Founder and CEO

Metabase

We immediately investigated the logs Metabase provided to us and confirmed that our database instance was accessed by the attacker. We confirmed that the following information was accessed:

  • Full name
  • Email address
  • Login IPs
  • Billing and shipping address information
    • Country
    • Address
    • City
    • State
    • Zip code
    • Phone number
    • Company

For Framework for Business customers, we are investigating whether the following information may additionally have been accessed:

  • Company
  • Phone
  • VAT
  • EIN
  • Billing Email

No other personally identifiable information, order information, or payment information was accessed.

Note that Metabase has additionally flagged:

Important: This is a preliminary update based on our current knowledge.

We are working with a third-party forensic investigation firm to understand the full nature and scope of the event.

We are providing you this interim update in advance of completing our investigation to allow you to better understand any potential impact and secure your data.

Our investigation is ongoing and the information shared now is preliminary.

Please look at the application logs as well as the queries executed that are provided as separate files in the zip file for detailed activity and a potential timeline.

We’re providing you notice of the breach in the meantime to ensure you have the earliest possible visibility. In the event Metabase notifies us of additional information that impacts you, we will send a follow-up email.

What was done to resolve the issue?

After we were notified of the breach by Metabase, we rotated credentials on all databases associated with our Metabase instance and confirmed that there were no changes in admin access or access to systems outside of Metabase.

What steps have you taken to ensure this doesn’t happen in the future?

We are evaluating the breadth and depth of data shared with business intelligence platforms, and scoping down their access to only the columns required for analysis.

Nirav Patel and the Framework Team

This sucks. I am glad they are fast at responding to this and I hope they will hash customer information.

item.description:
开发这个工具站是因为之前做一些 dApp 的时候，合约可能处于开发阶段或其他原因没有在 etherscan 等浏览器上 verify ，区块链浏览器无法根据 abi 解析合约信息和友好显示调用的参数等，只能看到不利于阅读的字符串。

但开发时我们可能拿到、或根据源码编译出 abi 文件，这个工具站的一大作用就是可以输入 abi ，然后根据 abi 进行合约读写等操作，以及解析 calldata 、selector 等。

之前没找到比较好的相关在线工具，就自己 vibe coding 了这个工具站，欢迎有需要的人使用和提出建议。

工具站地址： https://contractrw.dev

item.title: [V2EX] [生活] 彩礼，嫁女儿与卖女儿
item.description:
最近我稍微理解了国内彩礼的逻辑，彩礼这个习俗有好有坏。

男方给高额彩礼，然后女方父母回礼，并添一笔自己的钱 或是 房子 车子。 回礼 > 彩礼 = 嫁女儿 这种习俗就属于好习俗，类似于某种资金互助模式：双方父母一起出钱，帮助两个年轻人建立新的家庭。

而有些女方父母不做人的， 拿了男方彩礼，拿了男方的彩礼却基本不回礼。或是拿了 28 万 8 ，然后回礼 8 万，这种就属于卖女儿。

item.title: [V2EX] [程序员] 如果选 API 中转，你最在意便宜、稳定，还是可审计？
item.description:
最近看中转站相关讨论，发现很多推广帖都在卷价格和送额度，但我自己反而觉得这不是最核心的问题。 对开发者来说，便宜当然重要，但如果不知道请求有没有被记录、模型有没有被替换、上游不稳定时怎么处理，其实便宜也没什么意义。 想问下大家，如果真要选一个 API 中转服务，排序会是什么？ 价格低
稳定性
模型真实性
隐私和日志策略
售后响应
支持的模型数量 我个人目前倾向于：模型真实性 > 日志策略 > 稳定性 > 价格。 不知道 V 友们实际使用时是不是这么看。
